subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The Mini
description: Learn The Mini in one minute.

hook.text: The 1959 Mini was born from a fuel crisis. Designer Alec Issigonis had to fit four adults in 10 feet.

buildup.text: He turned the engine sideways—a radical idea that freed up 80% of the car's length for passengers.

discovery.text: The transverse engine layout worked so well that nearly every small car today uses the same design.

twist.text: Despite being a people's car, race-tuned Minis won the Monte Carlo Rally three times.

climax.text: Over 5.3 million were built. The Mini became a British icon alongside the Beatles and James Bond.

punchline.text: The smallest car changed how all small cars are built.

quiz.question: What was revolutionary about the Mini's engine placement?

details.summary: The original Mini, designed by Alec Issigonis in 1959, revolutionized small car design by turning the engine sideways and mounting the gearbox underneath it, maximizing cabin space from a tiny footprint.
details.whyItMatters: The Mini's transverse engine layout became the default for nearly all front-wheel-drive cars that followed. It proved that small cars could be fun, practical, and classless.
takeaways: Issigonis turned the engine 90 degrees to save space
Eighty percent of the car's floor was available for passengers
It won the Monte Carlo Rally three times in the 1960s

faq.question: How did the Mini influence modern car design?
faq.answer: Its transverse front-engine, front-wheel-drive layout was copied by virtually every small car manufacturer. Today over 80 percent of all cars sold worldwide use a variation of the layout Issigonis pioneered.

faq.question: Is the modern MINI related to the original?
faq.answer: BMW bought the brand and launched a completely new car in 2001. The modern MINI is larger, heavier, and more upmarket but preserves the go-kart handling feel and British character of the original.
